report:
### Conclusion

Based on evidence from large-scale randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and systematic reviews, **hydroxychloroquine does not reduce the likelihood of dying from COVID-19**.

Major clinical studies, including the landmark RECOVERY trial, evaluated hydroxychloroquine in hospitalized COVID-19 patients and found no significant reduction in 28-day mortality, length of hospital stay, or risk of mechanical ventilation compared to standard care (https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa2022926). 

Subsequent meta-analyses synthesizing results across thousands of participants in clinical trials similarly demonstrated no survival benefit for COVID-19 patients receiving hydroxychloroquine (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8013604/, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33859192/). Due to the clear lack of efficacy and potential risks—such as cardiac arrhythmias—regulatory agencies, including the U.S. FDA, revoked emergency use authorizations and advised against using hydroxychloroquine to treat COVID-19 (https://kffhealthnews.org/morning-breakout/fda-sends-strong-message-as-agency-yanks-emergency-use-approval-of-controversial-malaria-drug/).
